To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cap43 is a gene expressed in infiltrating macrophaes of human renal cell cancer.
the Cap43 gene is upregulated in the cancerous regions of human RCCs and that this is associated with the infiltration of macrophages.
the Cap43 gene is expressed in infiltrating macrophae in RCCs, and that the Cap43 mRNA is expressed in the epithelial cells of noncancerous renal tubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of human RCCs and the role of infiltrating macrophage in RCCs.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of human RCCs.
the expression of genes in human RCCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of Cap43 in macrophages is associated with the differentiation and activation of monocyte/macphage.
the Cap43 gene is expressed in infiltrating macrophae, but not in proliferating cancer cells of RCCs.
the Cap43 gene is a macrophage-associated gene, and that its expression is enhanced in the cancerous tissue of RCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cap43 gene is a candidate marker for macrophage infiltration in RCCs.
Cap43 mRNA is expressed in the epithelial cells of normal kidney and in the macrophages of renal cell carcinoma.
the Cap43 gene is highly expressed in infiltrating macrophae in RCCs and that this gene is a candidate for a new tumor marker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cap43 expression is upregulated in RCCs and is associated with macrophage infiltration, suggesting a potential role of Cap43 in RCCs.
the expression of the Cap 43 gene in infiltrated macrophages may reflect a specific macrophage activation state in RCCs.
Cap43 mRNA is expressed in the renal tubular epithelium in noncancer tissues and in infiltrating macroous macrophages in renal cell carcinomas.
